name: Create hostels table with ownership and identity fields
w: The hostel is the tenant. This table defines the ownership link that every RLS policy and every later query filters on, so it is the first business table to get right.
ac: hostels has id, owner_id, name, slug, type, phone, alt_phone, email, address, city, state, pincode, gstin, floors, status, created_at and updated_at (matching the Hostel domain type)
owner_id references profiles with an explicit delete rule
slug is generated server-side from the name with a collision suffix, and is unique across the whole platform
status supports draft, active and suspended
Indexes exist on owner_id and slug
profiles.hostel_id gets its foreign key to hostels in this migration
An owner can hold at most one draft hostel (partial unique index), so a double-submitted step 1 cannot create two drafts
out: No subscription, plan or billing fields yet.

name: Add hostel_id tenant scoping and enforce RLS policies
w: This is the multi-tenant guarantee for the entire product. If it fails, one hostel can read another hostel's residents, rooms and money, which ends the business rather than annoying one customer.
ac: RLS is enabled on hostels
A user sees only hostels they own or are staff of
Cross-hostel select, update and delete return zero rows or a hard error
Policies are proven with two distinct test users using the anon key
A reusable hostel-scoped policy pattern is documented for later tables
Membership is resolved by a SECURITY DEFINER helper (for example private.user_hostel_ids()) in a non-exposed schema with a fixed search_path, so policies never query RLS-protected tables recursively
The documented child-table pattern includes composite foreign keys (hostel_id, parent_id) so a row can never reference a parent in another hostel
These cases run in the cross-tenant RLS harness started by E9-T1
out: No per-attempt audit log of denied access in the MVP.

name: Build hostel onboarding step 1 with basic details and validation
w: This is the first screen a paying customer sees. It must feel short, validate immediately and never lose data if the owner abandons it, because setup often happens in gaps between other work.
ac: Captures hostel name, type (boys, girls or co-ed), contact phone and owner name
Inline field-level validation via the shared Zod schema
A draft hostel is persisted so the wizard can be resumed
Duplicate hostel name for the same owner warns before submission
Form values survive a page refresh
out: No document upload or verification in step 1.

name: Build hostel onboarding step 2 with address, contact and capacity
w: Address and capacity complete the hostel record and give the wizard a natural finish that flips the hostel from draft to active.
ac: Address, city, state and pincode captured with Indian pincode validation
Optional alternate contact supported
Declared number of floors captured
Back and forward navigation preserves previously entered data
Final submit transitions status from draft to active exactly once

name: Build hostel settings edit page
w: Hostels change: rent changes, phone numbers change, owners move. Without an edit path, early customers have to ask a developer to fix their own data.
ac: All non-identity fields are editable by the owner
Values are re-read from the database rather than patched in local state
updated_at is maintained automatically
Staff without permission receive a clear denial
Tampering with another hostel id in the request is blocked by RLS
out: No change history or approval workflow for edits.

name: Prevent duplicate hostels and handle incomplete onboarding resumes
w: Double submissions and abandoned wizards are the two fastest ways to end up with duplicate or orphaned hostel records in the first week of a new product.
ac: Database-level uniqueness guard on slug plus an owner and name check
Double-clicking submit creates exactly one hostel
An owner with an unfinished draft is redirected into the wizard from the dashboard
Incomplete records are discoverable rather than silently hidden
out: No automatic cleanup of long-abandoned drafts.

name: Implement hostel switcher for multi-hostel owners
w: Owners with more than one property, which is very common in Indian PG businesses, need to move between them without logging out or confusing the two.
ac: Owners with more than one hostel can switch the active hostel
The selection persists for the session
Every subsequent query is scoped to the active hostel
Switching cannot display cached data from the previously active hostel
The active hostel is kept in an httpOnly cookie and checked against membership on every request; a tampered value falls back to a hostel the user belongs to
RLS enforces membership; the active-hostel filter is applied by one shared query helper rather than repeated by hand
out: No consolidated multi-hostel reporting in the MVP.
